svg.title: Deep Point Forecasts vs Probabilistic Forecasts
svg.desc: Train on MSE and you get only the conditional mean; quantile losses, log-likelihoods and sample-based methods emit a distribution directly.
svg.text: Deep Point Forecasts vs Probabilistic Forecasts
Training to hit one mean vs training to emit quantiles or a distribution
A set of quantiles or parameters
How wrong it could be is nowhere in the output
It emits all the quantiles at once
The same model delivers the tail quantiles too
A symmetric loss calls out the mean
Over- and under-prediction are penalized equally
An asymmetric loss produces a quantile
Train several τ and you get a set of quantiles
Train on MSE and you get the conditional mean, with nothing in the tails.
If you want a distribution, change the loss first — training loss and evaluation metric must match.
Quantile loss, log-likelihood or sampling — whichever route, validate with PIT and coverage.
From classical to deep learning, the question is the same: what are you forecasting, and what are you scoring it with.
